 The Sub-Inspector of Police, Chennammanakere Achukattu Police Station, Bangalore has filed this chargesheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/s. 506, 504, 120B, 420 of I.P.C.
 2.The
criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Mano Sundar Vadivel.
M. The gist of the prosecution case is that Accused No.1 and 2 had taken a loan of Rs.3,04,217 to run a Poultry Farm business.

The accused failed to repay the same and as on 10-10-2014 the balance amount was Rs.
4,50,635.17/-.
The accused with an intention to cheat the complainant had closed the poultry farm.
When the CW1 to 3 went to recover the balance amount the Accused No.1 threatened to shoot the CW2 with revolver.
Later the complainant filed a private complaint before this court which came to be numbered as PCR No.16868/2014 and case was referred for investigation  3
C.C.No.15226/2015 U/Sec.156(3) of Cr.P.C which was registered as Crime No.69/2021 against the Accused for the aforesaid offences.

3. After completion of the investigation, the Sub-Inspector of Police, Chennammanakere Achukattu Police Station, Bangalore has filed this charge sheet against the Accused No.1 and 2 for the offence punishable U/s.506, 504, 120B, 420 of I.P.C.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took the cognizance of the alleged offence.

Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons Accused entered appearance and were enlarged on bail and the prosecution papers was provided to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.

Before framing charge, an opportunity of being heard was provided to the accused and after hearing them and the prosecution and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offence was framed and same was read over to the accused in the language known to them, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW1 and PW2 witnesses and got marked no documents.
The Statement of Accused as required U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C., was not recorded.
6. Heard arguments on both sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

7. The following point arise for my determination :-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that Accused have cheated the complainant by not  paying the amount and that the accused have abused  the CW1 to 3 in filthy language and also threatened CW2  to shoot with revolver and thereby the accused have  committed the offence punishable u/s.506, 504, 120B,
420 of I.P.C. .?
2) What Order?

8. My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1.......In the Negative.
 Point No.2.......As per final Order, for the following :-
 REASONS  9. POINT No.1:-
It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution will have to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubt.

In order to prove the same, the Manosundar Vadivel.M vs G Chandrashekar @ Chandrashekar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86671127/
3 prosecution has examined two witnesses as PW1 and 2 and no documents are marked.

sentences.text: 10. CW2 was examined as PW1.
He has deposed that when he had been to the house of the accused to recover the balance amount the Accused No.1 had threatened him of shooting him with revolver.
During his cross examination he has deposed that he had  5  C.C.No.15226/2015 permission to go to the house of the accused.
He has deposed that he alone had gone to recover the amount.
11.Though CW3 was examined as PW2 but he never turned up for further chief examination.
Hence, he was dropped.
As the witness never turned up for further chief and also cross his evidence cannot be looked into.
12. In this case the only evidence available on record is the evidence of PW1.
Though he states he had gone to the house of the accused to recover the amount but to show the same no letter of deputation or authority is on record.
Hence, the version of the witness cannot be believed.
When the prosecution has failed to prove the presence of PW1 on the spot on the alleged date of incident then the entire case of the prosecution has no legs to stand on.
In this case the prosecution has not even able to secure the complainant.
It is the case of the PW1 that he was not authorized to give complaint so he did not give the complaint.
This is hard to believe for the reason that he was insulted and threatened in personal capacity.

When such being the case the non Manosundar Vadivel.M vs G Chandrashekar @ Chandrashekar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86671127/
4 filing of the complaint by PW1 and subsequent filing of complaint  6  C.C.No.15226/2015 with unexplained delay by CW1 casts doubt on the case of the prosecution.

sentences.text: Further, though the prosecution has contended that the accused had played fraud on the bank by taking loan and not repaying the same, but to show the same no documents are brought on record.
For all the above discussion I give benefit of doubt to the accused herein and this court holds that prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly I answer point No.1 in the Negative.

13. POINT No.2:- In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
 ORDER
In exercise of power conferred U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C., accused No.1 and 2 are acquitted of the offence punishable U/s.506, 504, 120B, 420 of I.P.C.
The bail bond and surety bonds executed by the accused No.1 and 2 shall remain in force for 6 months.
